paper.title_en: HETDEX [OII] galaxies at $z \le 0.48$: Growth of structures from power spectrum multipoles
paper.abstract_en: We use the monopole and quadrupole power spectra of [\ionO2]-emitting galaxies in the HETDEX Public Data Release 1 to constrain the growth of cosmic structures at $z\le0.48$. We interpret the power spectra using a simulation-based model built from the Mucho-Uchuu-1G $N$-body simulation. The best-fit model reproduces the observed power spectra remarkably well up to $k_\mathrm{max}=0.7~h~\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$, and goodness-of-fit tests confirm that the HETDEX [\ionO2] clustering is consistent with the \textit{Planck} flat $Λ$CDM cosmology. We test the general relativity (GR) prediction for the linear growth index, $γ\simeq 0.55$. When the Alcock-Paczyński parameters are held fixed at their fiducial values, we find consistency with the GR prediction, $γ=0.55\pm 0.05$. And, when the AP parameters are allowed to vary, $γ=0.60\pm 0.07$, which is consistent with both the GR prediction and the suppressed growth rate reported by \citet{Nguyen_2023}. These results establish HETDEX [\ionO2] galaxies as a competitive, independent low-redshift probe of the growth of structures and motivate future full cosmological inference.
